solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: College writer banks money

indicators.note: the writer's name lines both sides of the money, as banks flank a river

parts.note: Albert Camus, the French author of The Outsider
P stands for penny or pence, British money

explanation.surface: An author with a stash of cash on either side of him at university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'banks' is a verb here: CAMUS sits on both sides of P.
explanation.definitionFit: A campus is the grounds of a university or college, so it can stand for the institution itself.

clue.text: God's appearance in Cameron's film

definitions.meaning: in Hindu belief, the earthly incarnation a deity takes
James Cameron's 2009 blockbuster set on Pandora

explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share one word: a deity's earthly incarnation, and the title of the James Cameron science-fiction epic.

clue.text: Staff training run by Dicky Nelson

parts.note: PE is physical education, school exercise training
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for a run

indicators.note: dicky means shaky or unsound, so the name's letters are knocked out of order

explanation.surface: Admiral Nelson, in poor health, puts the crew through their exercises.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dicky' is British slang for shaky or unsound, used here as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Personnel are the people employed by an organisation, its workforce or staff.

clue.text: Boring person with share of loot is shot

parts.note: a square is a conventional, dull person
a cut is one's portion of the proceeds

explanation.surface: A dull criminal takes his slice of the haul and gets shot.
explanation.walkthrough: A SQUARE CUT is a cricket stroke hitting the ball square of the wicket on the off side; 'shot' looks like gunfire but means a batting stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, this is a named batting stroke played with a horizontal bat to a short wide delivery.

clue.text: One is to take some money round for this noblewoman

indicators.note: the bars of bullion go round the contracted phrase, enclosing it

parts.note: bars of gold or silver bullion serve as a store of money
contracted to one's, giving these letters without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: A woman gets her title by gathering some cash about her.
explanation.walkthrough: The blog notes the newspaper printed 'silver' where this version says 'money'; ingots work as either, and 'round' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A baroness is a woman holding the rank of baron, a member of the nobility.

clue.text: Czechs seen here half-eaten by snake

indicators.note: the half prefix is swallowed inside the snake

parts.note: a boa is a constrictor snake
hemi- is the prefix meaning half

explanation.surface: Something has been half-swallowed by a serpent where the Czechs live.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-eaten' looks like one word but splits: 'half' is the inserted piece and 'eaten by' signals the containment.
explanation.definitionFit: Bohemia is the historic western region of the Czech Republic, homeland of the Czech people.

clue.text: Royal birds for doomed wolfsuckling

parts.note: R abbreviates royal, as in RN
emus are large flightless Australian birds

explanation.surface: A regal flock of birds is meant for an ill-fated child raised by a wolf.
explanation.walkthrough: Romulus and Remus were twins suckled by a she-wolf; Romulus killed his brother.
explanation.definitionFit: In Roman legend this twin, nursed by a she-wolf, was slain by his brother at Rome's founding.

clue.text: Girl not entirely conventional

indicators.note: the synonym is cut short by its final letter

parts.note: normal means ordinary or conventional

explanation.surface: A young woman who is a bit unorthodox.
explanation.definitionFit: Norma is a woman's given name, also Bellini's operatic heroine.

clue.text: Third from Massenet with Panurge to reveal some deep device

indicators.note: takes the third letter of the composer's name
the opera title is opened up and rearranged to show a new word

explanation.surface: Massenet and his opera Panurge conjure something from the depths.
explanation.walkthrough: Panurge is a Massenet opera, which makes the surface plausible; its letters rearranged after S give PEARGUN.
explanation.definitionFit: A speargun fires harpoons underwater, so it is an implement used deep in the sea by divers.

clue.text: Festival beauty with her wings unfurled

indicators.note: unfurling spreads things out of their folded order, so the letters are rearranged
the wings of a word are its outer letters

explanation.surface: A lovely woman spreads her wings at a festival.
explanation.walkthrough: 'her wings' gives H and R, shuffled with BEAUTY.
explanation.definitionFit: Bayreuth in Bavaria hosts the annual Wagner opera festival, so the town names the event.

clue.text: Situation causing hardship for lot of crows

definitions.meaning: informally, something very hard to bear, as in 'the traffic was hell'
the traditional collective noun for a flock of crows

explanation.definitionFit: The word is slang for an ordeal, and also the collective term for a group of these black birds.

clue.text: Prefer 4 over very good 5

indicators.note: the number word is laid over the letters, enclosing them

parts.note: the number written as a word
A is the top grade, meaning very good
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Choose four ahead of a very good five.
explanation.walkthrough: The figures look like cross-references to other clues, but they are plain numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: To favour something is to prefer it or show partiality towards it.

clue.text: Complete defeat where service engineer admits car tampered with

indicators.note: lets in, so the shuffled car goes inside

parts.note: Mass is a church service
E is an abbreviation for engineer

indicators.note: meddled with, so the word car is rearranged

explanation.surface: A mechanic at church takes in a car that has been interfered with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tampered with' is the anagram signal, and 'admits' puts the result inside the service-plus-engineer pair.
explanation.definitionFit: A massacre in sport or war is a crushing, one-sided rout.

clue.text: Queen leaves grave to weep convulsively

indicators.note: the queen departs, so those letters drop out

parts.note: sober means serious or grave
ER, Elizabeth Regina

explanation.surface: The monarch walks away from a tomb to cry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'grave' looks like a burial place but is the adjective, serious.
explanation.definitionFit: To sob is to cry with noisy, heaving breaths.

clue.text: In Clubman I soon lost safe driving dividend

indicators.note: the letters have lost their way and are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A club member loses something in an insurance matter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; CLUBMAN I SOON is the fodder. A no-claim bonus is a British insurance discount for years without a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: Motor insurers reward claim-free years with this premium discount, a payoff for careful motoring.

clue.text: Structures that loom where Hamlet is closer to king in breakdown

indicators.note: broken down, so the letters are rearranged
the closing letter of the word

explanation.surface: Hamlet draws near the king while having a breakdown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'closer to king' gives G, mixed with HAMLET IS; 'closer' means the end, not nearer.
explanation.definitionFit: Megaliths are huge standing stones, like those of Stonehenge, that tower over the landscape.

clue.text: See 28
Military rule in world was disastrous

indicators.note: a disaster wrecks order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Martial law was a calamity across the globe.
explanation.definitionFit: Sword-law is government by force of arms, the rule of the military.

clue.text: Thing worked out after musical interval determines what you will play!

parts.note: a twelfth spans an octave plus a fifth

indicators.note: solved, so the letters of thing are rearranged

explanation.surface: A thing is resolved after an interval in music.
explanation.walkthrough: Shakespeare's comedy is subtitled 'Or What You Will', so the play is 'what you will' itself; 'determines' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's comedy carries the alternative title What You Will, so it is that play.

clue.text: As Bunter starts with fork and trifle

indicators.note: takes the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A greedy schoolboy dives in with a fork and dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Billy Bunter is the greedy, plump schoolboy of British comics; trifle is a layered British dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Billy Bunter is famously plump, so this adjective describes him.

clue.text: Most tidy take food into cosy place

indicators.note: the eating goes inside the nest

parts.note: a nest is a snug home
to eat

explanation.surface: Consume a meal in a snug spot as neatly as possible.
explanation.definitionFit: Neatest is the superlative of neat, meaning most orderly.

clue.text: Noted German losing love vanished during hostilities

indicators.note: placed within the period of the fighting

parts.note: war is armed hostility

indicators.note: drops the letter for love

parts.note: gone means disappeared
O, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A famous German lost his sweetheart amid the fighting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means famous but also hints at music notes: Wagner the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Richard Wagner was a celebrated German composer, so a noted figure in music.

clue.text: Easier to produce three tragedies for Aeschylus

indicators.note: the fodder words are reworked to produce a new word

explanation.surface: Writing tragedies became simpler for the Greek dramatist.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oresteia is the trilogy by Aeschylus: Agamemnon, The Libation Bearers and The Eumenides.

clue.text: Unimportant manuscript turned up in its entirety

indicators.note: in a down clue the abbreviation reads upwards, reversed

parts.note: all means the whole

explanation.surface: A complete manuscript has been found.
explanation.definitionFit: Small means minor or insignificant.

clue.text: Presidential quarters for the oil family?

parts.note: for a president, the East side of the White House
a wing of a building is a set of rooms

explanation.surface: The White House's private rooms are given to a family of oilmen.
explanation.walkthrough: The East Wing is part of the White House. The Ewings were the Texas oil dynasty in the TV soap Dallas.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ewings of the long-running soap Dallas were a rich Texan oil clan.

clue.text: Room for movement in Spooner's little song

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the starting sounds of words

parts.note: wee is Scots for small
a lay is a ballad or song

explanation.surface: A tiny tune gives some freedom of manoeuvre.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeway is margin or freedom to act or move.

clue.text: No time to talk with boxer in compound

indicators.note: means without, so the time letter is removed

parts.note: taken as written
T is the physics abbreviation for time
Muhammad Ali, the heavyweight champion

explanation.surface: No time to chat with the fighter at his compound.
explanation.walkthrough: 'compound' looks like an enclosure, but it is a chemical compound.
explanation.definitionFit: An alkali is a chemical compound that neutralises acids.

clue.text: FTSE in collapse all about, so working at once

indicators.note: the reworked index letters go right around the rest
the index has collapsed, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
on, as a machine switched on and running

explanation.surface: The stock index crashes, and everyone is busy at once.
explanation.walkthrough: FTSE is the London share index; 'in collapse' makes EFTS, which goes 'all about' SO and ON.
explanation.definitionFit: Eftsoons is an archaic word meaning soon afterwards or forthwith.

clue.text: Googled this with FT after struggle to find work from 21 that 9 would produce

indicators.note: the words have been through a struggle, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone searched online with the newspaper's help after a tussle to find an opera.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is WAGNER and 9 is BAYREUTH, whose festival stages his operas.
explanation.definitionFit: Götterdämmerung, final opera of Wagner's Ring cycle, is staged at his Bayreuth festival.

clue.text: Canaanite commander to emphasise racial content

indicators.note: what is contained within the words

explanation.surface: Instruction to stress racial matter.
explanation.walkthrough: Sisera was the Canaanite general defeated by Deborah and Barak in the Book of Judges.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible, Sisera led the Canaanite army of King Jabin.
